artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan for the books record-editing rule file, the record-maintenance diagnostics context file, the lean4 README pointer, and registration across three surfaces in two extensions.

memory_candidates.content: Adding a NEW rule file to an agent-system extension requires three distinct registration surfaces, not one: (1) manifest.json's provides.rules array -- check-extension-docs.sh Rule H (check_undeclared_rules) FAILS on a rule file present on disk but absent from provides.rules, so this is a hard gate failure, not cosmetic; (2) EXTENSION.md, which Rule U caps at 60 lines with no per-extension exemption, so a pointer addition to a file already at the cap must be offset by an equal trim in that same file; (3) for a new CONTEXT file (not a rule), index-entries.json, whose line_count is checked for exact accuracy by Rule R -- never hand-type it, run generate-context-line-counts.sh --write after all content is final. provides.context is a DIRECTORY-level reference ('project/<ext>') and auto-covers new context files; provides.rules is filename-literal and does not. A cross-extension pointer line (extension A's README pointing into extension B's corpus, against the dependency arrow) additionally desyncs A's own index-entries line_count, so the --write sweep must cover both extensions.
